results.goal: Step up to the next role
results.headline: You build clean, well-structured models and you already think about how other disciplines will use them. Coordination is the natural next step.

review.stem: A wall in your model has no material, no fire rating and no manufacturer, but its geometry is exact. What kind of data is it missing?
review.feedback: Right. Geometry says what shape it is; alphanumeric (property) data says what it is and how it performs.
review.lesson_title: Explain geometric vs alphanumeric data in model objects

review.stem: A client asks for 'LOD 350' on ductwork at stage 3. Under ISO 19650 what should you actually be checking?
options: That every duct is modelled to fabrication detail
The Level of Information Need for that deliverable and purpose
That the model is under 200 MB
review.feedback: Level of Information Need is purpose-driven: geometric detail, alphanumeric data and documentation are specified separately for each exchange. Over-modelling wastes effort.
review.lesson_title: Apply the correct Level of Information Need to geometric outputs

review.stem: You need to share your Revit model with a structural engineer who works in Tekla. What is the most robust approach?
options: Export to IFC using an agreed MVD
review.feedback: IFC via an agreed Model View Definition keeps geometry and properties readable in any openBIM tool. DWG drops the object data.
review.lesson_title: Export native models to open formats (IFC, NWC)

review.stem: In a federated Navisworks model you need to find every pipe on Level 3 that crosses the atrium. Which tool do you reach for first?
review.feedback: Yes. Selection tree filters by discipline and level, and a section box isolates the zone so you can see it.

review.stem: What does the suitability code 'S2' on a shared container tell the person downloading it?
options: It is shared for information only
review.feedback: S2 means 'suitable for information' in the ISO 19650 UK annex, and S1 is coordination. Naming and status codes tell the team what they can safely do with a file.
review.lesson_title: Upload/download files with correct naming conventions and suitability codes

review.stem: Your BEP fixes the project base point at grid A/1 with a 0 m level datum. A linked model arrives 300 m off. What do you do?
options: Ask the author to re-issue to the BEP origin and shared coordinates
Ignore it, Navisworks will fix it
review.feedback: Correct. Never fix another discipline's coordinates locally; the BEP origin is the contract everyone models to.
review.lesson_title: Model to the BEP's origin points, phasing rules and milestones

review.stem: A clash report lists 400 hard clashes between ducts and beams. What is the first useful thing to do?
options: Assign all 400 to the MEP engineer
Group and de-duplicate them into a handful of real issues
Re-run the test with a bigger tolerance
review.feedback: Right. Hundreds of raw clashes usually collapse into a few root causes once grouped by location and system.
review.lesson_title: Group, filter and de-duplicate clash results for review

review.stem: Your coordinator asks how far along your model is. Which reply is most useful?
options: 'Levels 1–3 modelled to LOIN, level 4 blocked on the structural grid, façade assumed'
review.feedback: Exactly. Progress, blockers and assumptions — in one line.
review.lesson_title: Communicate model status honestly: progress, blockers, assumptions

roadmap.goal: Step up to the next role
roadmap.summary: You placed at Production (Builder). Your goal is 'Move up to the next phase', so this plan takes you to Coordination. It starts by closing 3 gaps from your assessment, then works through Technical & Computational Proficiency, Information Management & Open Standards, Process Execution & Coordination and Interpersonal & Supportive Competencies at Production and Coordination level. About 4h of lessons at 60 min/week — roughly 4 weeks.

milestones.title: Close the gaps from your assessment
milestones.why: Three answers pointed at skills you nearly have. Fix those first and everything after gets easier.

items.title: Apply the correct Level of Information Need to geometric outputs
Export native models to open formats (IFC, NWC)
Upload/download files with correct naming conventions and suitability codes

milestones.title: Production: Technical & Computational Proficiency
milestones.why: Solid authoring, data and federation habits are what Coordinators rely on from their modelers.

items.title: Create parametric model elements from project templates
Manage worksets and model subdivision in shared models
Coordinate shared coordinates and base points across models
Enrich objects with parameters, materials and metadata
Apply classification codes to elements per project standard
Prepare models for federation: purge, coordinates and export settings
Navigate a federated 3D model viewer
Revit basics for architecture

milestones.title: Production: Information Management & Open Standards
milestones.why: Know where files live, how they are named and how they leave your authoring tool.

items.title: Link and reference shared models correctly from the CDE
Export IFC files using predefined Model View Definitions (MVDs)
Read a LOIN table and model to the specified need

milestones.title: Coordination: Process Execution & Coordination
milestones.why: This is the core of the Coordinator role: reading, fixing and closing out clashes to the BEP.

items.title: Read a clash report: locations, elements and status codes
Fix assigned discipline clashes in native authoring software
Verify resolved clashes and close out assigned issues
Complete BEP-required checks before each model issue
Extract documentation, schedules and quantity take-offs from a coordinated model

milestones.title: Coordination: Technical & Computational Proficiency
milestones.why: Run the checks yourself instead of waiting for someone else's report.

items.title: Run rule-based clash detection (Navisworks / Solibri)
Validate model integrity: duplicates, overlaps and orphaned elements
Run pre-built Dynamo scripts for repetitive tasks

milestones.title: Coordination: Interpersonal & Supportive Competencies
milestones.why: Coordinators spend half their week in meetings. Make those minutes count.

items.title: Write coordination minutes that drive accountable actions
Communicate model status honestly: progress, blockers, assumptions

goals_suggested.title: Close my assessment gaps
goals_suggested.description: Finish the three lessons that cover the questions you missed.

goals_suggested.title: Finish Production: Technical & Computational Proficiency
goals_suggested.description: Complete every lesson in your first milestone, including the Revit basics course.

goals_suggested.title: Reach Coordination level
goals_suggested.description: Work through the whole plan and land at Coordinator.
